title: Alibi and Will Again
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Halloway is found empty during a centennial exhumation, insurance investigator Theo Lockridge is pulled into a case that unravels forty years of Halloway's carefully constructed legend. Theo's photographic memory catches a detail everyone else missed: a witness signature on an old policy, dated three days after the man supposedly died. Hunting the 'dead' witness—a woman named Vera who faked her death to escape Halloway—Theo uncovers that the founder staged his own death to flee embezzlement charges, and that several townspeople have been quietly protecting the lie for decades. As Theo closes in, someone begins killing those who might talk, and Theo realizes their own invisibility was engineered by the same conspiracy. In the end, Theo must choose between exposing the truth and sparing the one person who showed them love, ultimately publishing the evidence while giving Vera a head start—and finally stepping out of the shadows themselves.
about_author: Rosalind Joubert spent fifteen years as a claims adjuster in small-town New England before turning to fiction, drawing on a career spent reading the fine print of other people's tragedies. She writes from a converted boathouse where she keeps, she admits, far too many unsolved case files.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Theo Lockridge, attending the centennial exhumation as an insurer's formality. When the coffin lid opens to reveal nothing but weighted sandbags, the crowd's grief curdles into confusion. Theo privately notes the coffin's unusual weight distribution. Emotional beat: quiet vindication—the invisible investigator finally sees something no one else can explain.

chapters.title: A Memory Like Ledger Paper
chapters.summary: Flashback-woven chapter establishing Theo's photographic memory through their recall of three 'accidents' they quietly proved were murders. Police chief Dana Okafor grudgingly asks for help. POV: Theo, first person. Emotional beat: loneliness of a mind that never forgets, and the fragile trust being offered.

chapters.title: The Signature That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: In the Halloway estate archives, Theo finds a 1984 life policy co-signed by 'Vera Ashcombe'—dated three days after Halloway's recorded death. The archivist, elderly Mr. Pell, goes pale and asks Theo to forget it. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the first crack in the town's marble legend; dread mixed with exhilaration.

chapters.title: Everyone Loved Edmund
chapters.summary: Multi-POV mosaic: townsfolk recounting Halloway's generosity at a memorial vigil. Each anecdote contains a small inconsistency Theo files away. A teenage girl, Cass, mentions her grandmother 'knew Vera.' POV shifts among five residents. Emotional beat: the suffocating warmth of collective myth-making.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Drowned Twice
chapters.summary: Theo researches Vera Ashcombe: officially drowned in 1984, body recovered, buried. But the coroner's file has a page missing—Theo remembers seeing its ghost impression years ago. POV: Theo, with a brief interlude from Chief Okafor doubting herself. Emotional beat: the past pushing back against memory itself.

chapters.title: Fine Print
chapters.summary: At Meridian Insurance's regional office, Theo discovers the company paid out on Halloway's death despite irregularities—and that the claim was approved by Theo's own late mentor, Ruth Calloway. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: betrayal; the personal cost of a truth that implicates the dead.

chapters.title: What Cass Knew
chapters.summary: Theo interviews Cass's grandmother, Ida, who nearly confesses before her son interrupts and orders Theo out. That night Ida's house is ransacked. POV alternates Theo and Ida. Emotional beat: fear spreading like water damage through an old house.

chapters.title: The Second Accident
chapters.summary: Mr. Pell dies when his archive ladder 'fails'—the third staged accident of Theo's career, now aimed at this case. Theo recognizes the rigging instantly. POV: Theo, then Okafor confronting her own department's inertia. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve; the killer has stopped being careful.

chapters.title: Ruth's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Searching Ruth Calloway's effects, Theo finds an unfinished letter naming 'E.H.' and mentioning a lake house under another name. Someone has already searched the room—but missed the letter sewn into a coat lining. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: tenderness toward a dead mentor who tried to make amends.

chapters.title: The Lake House
chapters.summary: Theo traces the property to a shell corporation and finds the cabin recently lived in: fresh coffee, a woman's coat, a burned document in the grate with one legible word—'witness.' POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the hunt becoming real; Vera is alive and close.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Small Town
chapters.summary: Okafor reveals pressure from above to close the exhumation as vandalism. She and Theo form an uneasy alliance off the books. POV: Okafor primarily. Emotional beat: two lonely professionals choosing each other over institutions.

chapters.title: Forty Years of Sundays
chapters.summary: Ida, emboldened by Pell's death, tells Theo the truth she's carried: she helped Vera fake her drowning because Halloway was going to kill her. But she swears Halloway himself arranged his own empty coffin later. POV: Ida. Emotional beat: the relief and terror of confession.

chapters.title: The Man in the Photograph
chapters.summary: Theo's memory flags a recurring background figure in decades of town photos—an unaging man watching parades. Facial reconstruction suggests Halloway alive well into the 2000s. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: vertigo; the dead man has been home all along.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading My Mail
chapters.summary: Theo returns home to find everything exactly one inch displaced—someone testing whether they notice. A note: 'You were safer invisible.' Theo realizes their obscurity was curated. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: violation; the hunter learning they were also the kept.

chapters.title: Vera
chapters.summary: Theo stakes out the lake house and finally meets Vera Ashcombe, sharp and unrepentant. She confirms Halloway embezzled the founding trust and staged his death to escape exposure—but insists she's been hiding from him, not the law. POV: alternating Theo and Vera. Emotional beat: recognition between two people who survived by disappearing.

chapters.title: The Third Death Wasn't Staged
chapters.summary: Forensics on Pell's ladder reveal a second set of prints: Halloway's grandson Martin, the estate lawyer, has been cleaning up the family myth—and silencing witnesses—with his grandfather directing him by letter. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: horror that the legend reproduced itself in flesh.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Theo lets slip a false location for Vera through Ida, betting Martin will move. The trap half-works: Martin comes, but so does a fire set to destroy the lake house evidence. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: guilt—using Ida as bait nearly costs a life.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Martin corners Theo and offers the thing Theo secretly wants: erasure, anonymity, protection—in exchange for silence about Vera. He reveals Ruth died securing the evidence Theo now carries. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the temptation to vanish again, weighed against love for the truth.

chapters.title: Coffin Empty, Town Full
chapters.summary: Okafor arrests Martin after Theo's recorded confrontation, but Halloway—if alive—is still out there, and Vera refuses to testify. The town fractures between those who want the myth and those who want the truth. POV: rotating ensemble. Emotional beat: a community choosing what to remember.

chapters.title: The Founder's Grave
chapters.summary: Climax: a final letter lures Theo to the original grave site at night. Edmund Halloway, old and dying, appears—not to threaten, but to ask to be forgotten. Theo instead records his confession as he collapses. Martin, escaped custody briefly, tries to intervene and is stopped by Okafor. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the monster revealed as a tired man, which is somehow worse.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Resolution begins: Halloway's recorded confession clears Vera legally; she chooses to stay and face the town rather than run. Ida is honored, not punished. Theo publishes the full account—including their own manipulated history—under their real name for the first time. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the cost and release of being seen.

chapters.title: Alibi and Will Again
chapters.summary: Epilogue, one year later: the reburial of an honest, empty coffin with a new stone reading only 'Edmund Halloway, 1921–1984, and whatever remained.' Vera tends Ida's garden; Okafor runs unopposed for sheriff; Theo takes on a new 'accident' case, visibly, publicly, remembered. Final line echoes the title: an alibi is just a will to be elsewhere. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: peace earned, not given.
